articles.title: Anthony Joshua knocks out Kristian Prenga after huge scare to move closer to blockbuster showdown with Tyson Fury
articles.summary: Anthony Joshua's clash with Tyson Fury looked in doubt after he was floored inside 20 seconds of fight with Kristian Prenga, only to rebound by knocking out Albanian in second round; Fury and Joshua now set to meet in November, with contracts signed but no venue announced yet
articles.body:
Joshua endured a dismal first three minutes on Saturday night, hitting the canvas twice, firstly from a vicious uppercut, with the Albanian knockout specialist eyeing a seismic shock.

However, Prenga was demolished by right hands soon after in AJ's first outing since he was a passenger in a car crash in December that killed friends Sina Ghami and Latif 'Latz' Ayodele.

An emotional Joshua dedicated his win to his late team members, saying: "It's more than punch power. That was spirit, that was Latz, that was Sina, that was the families. It hurts to even talk about it. It has been tough. It's my brothers. I don't want to talk about it."

Fury had completed his own stoppage victory on Friday , over Polish veteran Mariusz Wach in a non-televised bout fought in front of a small crowd in Thailand, before vowing not to travel to Saudi Arabia for a face-off with Joshua , who he could now box in November.

There was no sign of Fury as Joshua overcame a boxer in Prenga who had recorded each of his 20 victories via knockout and won his previous 16 contests since a first career defeat in February 2017.

Prenga's stats made for strong reading and although there were no huge names on his CV he threatened a stunning result - one that could have shattered hopes of Joshua facing Fury - before the Brit registered his 30th win in 34 fights and second in a row, having beaten Jake Paul last year weeks before his car crash.

After a hiccup-free weekend for Fury and Joshua coming through early adversity, a long-awaited all-British scrap looks set to happen in the autumn, with contracts already signed.

It could possibly be staged at 2am UK time at Wembley Stadium to suit a global audience but Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has said America is the preferred venue for fight organiser Turki Alalshikh.

If and when this clash does take place - Fury questioned whether Joshua would have the "guts" to challenge him as he spoke after dismissing Wach - boxing fans will get what they have wanted for years and, at various points, doubted they would ever see.

Fears of Joshua suffering a fifth pro defeat, after two losses to Oleksandr Usyk - the same as Fury - and one each to Daniel Dubois and Andy Ruiz, were rampant after his shocking start against Prenga but his flurry of heavy blows in the second round earned him victory.

On Fury, Joshua added: "I am going to rip his heart out. I am the meanest and most vicious champion there has ever been!

"All jokes aside, I respect everything he has done and achieved but we are here now. I hope the fans will be in for a lovely treat."

Joshua also reserved praise for Prenga, saying: "He's a strong guy and I think Eddie [Hearn] wants to sign him now!

"He is going to do well and has a bright future. Maybe with a bit more experience, he will be up there with the rest of us.

"He is strong and durable and gave me a good test but this is what champions do, we rise. We get knocked down and stand up. That's life."

articles.title: Anthony Joshua remembers late friends after win over Kristian Prenga sets up Tyson Fury fight and 'lovely treat' for fans
articles.summary: Anthony Joshua says he "will not be stopped" after coming through almighty scare to beat Kristian Prenga; Tyson Fury set to be next for AJ; promoter Eddie Hearn hails  Joshua's character as he recovers from first-round knockdowns in first fight since friends' deaths in December car crash
articles.body:
Joshua knocked out Albanian heavyweight Prenga in the second round in Jeddah on Saturday night, after twice being floored himself in the first, including just 20 seconds into the contest.

The British star displayed tremendous character to battle back from the brink of defeat, a trait he has had to show in abundance since the deaths of team members Sina Ghami and Latif 'Latz' Ayodele in a car crash in December in which he was a passenger.

Speaking after overcoming Prenga, Joshua told DAZN : "It's more than punch power. That was spirit, that was Latz, that was Sina, that was the families. It hurts to even talk about it.

"It has been tough. It's my brothers. I don't want to talk about it."

Joshua: I respect everything Fury has done

Joshua was able to discuss Fury, with the British boxers now set to end over a decade of circling each other by locking horns in November, with America seemingly the most likely destination.

Fury beat Polish veteran Mariusz Wach in his own tune-up fight in Thailand on Friday.

AJ added of his countryman, who did not head to Saudi Arabia for a face-off with his rival: "I am going to rip his heart out. I am the meanest and most vicious champion there has ever been!

"All jokes aside, I respect everything he has done and achieved but we are here now. I hope the fans will be in for a lovely treat.

"I've learnt I can't be stopped. I won't be stopped and I won't be denied. We're here and we're coming. Trust me."

'No one can imagine what Joshua has been through'

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn confirmed that contracts have been signed for the blockbuster showdown before going on to praise his fighter's "astonishing" return to the ring after the "grief and pain" he had to deal with following the car crash shortly before Christmas.

Hearn said of Joshua on DAZN : "To be honest with you, tonight is all about the strength AJ has showed to even be here tonight - and the strength in that fight.

"No one can imagine what he has been through in the last seven months. During the first round, I was thinking, 'we came back too soon'.

"I feel boxing once saved him and I feel like he needed boxing to help him get through this. That camp allowed him to focus while he was facing so much grief and pain.

"He is a strong man and he likes to deal with his problems on his own - I'm not saying that is the right way but that is his way to do it. To even be in the ring tonight was astonishing.

"When you go down a couple ​of times in the first round and you're looking like ​your career might be over, he had to go to the depths one more time to get ‌up and fight on."

Watch Edgar Berlanga vs Steven Butler and Richardson Hitchins vs Ricardo Salas, in New York, live on Sky Sports Action and Sky Sports Main Event from 10pm Sunday. Stream boxing with NOW.

articles.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Everything you need to know about the proposed heavyweight fight
articles.summary: Tyson Fury stopped Mariusz Wach in Thailand on Friday before Anthony Joshua climbed off the canvas twice to knock out Kristian Prenga in Jeddah on Saturday; contracts are signed for the all-British showdown, which is targeted for November, with a date and venue still to be announced
articles.body:
Fury and Joshua have shared eras, headlines and negotiating tables without ever sharing a ring. A fight was previously announced for August 2021 in Saudi Arabia and terms were accepted again for a December 2022 date before both collapsed without a punch being thrown.

This weekend's return to the ring for both men is expected to be the final box-ticking exercise before it happens for real this time.

What happened in Fury and AJ's warm-up fights?

Fury claimed a seventh-round TKO over Mariusz Wach at the Max Muay Thai Stadium in Thailand on Friday, with Wach signalling to his corner to wave the fight off before the officials ended it ahead of the eighth.

The bout was not televised and fought in front of around 1,500 spectators in Pattaya and was the 37-year-old Fury's second since ending his latest retirement, following his points win over Arslanbek Makhmudov at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in April.

Joshua's night in Jeddah was far more dramatic . He was floored inside 20 seconds by Kristian Prenga, hit the canvas twice in the first round, then knocked out the Albanian with right hands in the second.

It was AJ's first outing since he was a passenger in a December car crash that killed his friends Sina Ghami and Latif Ayodele and his first fight since stopping Jake Paul last December.

The calendar has been circled for November and the warm-up double-header was arranged to align with that timeline.

Contracts are signed and the pair are now set to meet, though a precise date has not been announced – although Fury said after beating Wach that he hopes the fight is signed "next week".

Turki Alalshikh, who is promoting the fight, has said he wants the fight to suit a global audience and that he will talk to London authorities over a later-than-usual start time.

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has revealed that the USA is now the preferred venue for Alalshikh, but highlighted that the current signed contracts state that the fight must be in the UK.

"That doesn't tally up with the contract that we signed," he said. "Until we're happy, we expect every point of that contract to be followed. I feel like this fight should be taking place in the UK.

"If they want to change the contract, then we have to renegotiate the contract. Which, by the way, is not a problem but it's a conversation we have to have."

Wembley has been championed by Barry Hearn, Eddie's dad, while Cardiff's Principality Stadium has been rumoured but Croke Park appears not to be an option despite earlier suggestions of talks about moving the bout to Dublin.

"There's two or three different places it could be but there's still objections to a few of them and the one man who's going to make the decisions is Turki Alalshikh, and Netflix," said Spencer Brown, Fury's manager.

"They're going to make the decisions. They both want the fight, so there's going to be a bit of chopping and changing."

"I am going to rip his heart out," Joshua said after beating Prenga. "All jokes aside, I respect everything he has done and achieved but we are here now.

"I hope the fans will be in for a lovely treat."

He also dedicated the win on Saturday to his late friends, adding: "It's more than just punch power, it was spirit."

Joshua has also insisted the contract states the fight must be in the UK.

Fury got his shots in after beating Wach and questioned whether Joshua has the "guts" to face him , referencing his rival declining to enter the ring after the Makhmudov fight in front of 70,000 at Tottenham.

"The biggest test of it all is how big his ***** are," said Fury.

"I think he's a big s********. In Tottenham in front of 70,000 people, he never had the guts to get in the ring and face me.

"Let's see if he ever does, I'm not convinced."

Fury then reeled off Vegas, New York, Ireland, London, Belfast and even Pattaya as possible venues.

That followed his Sky Sports News interview in fight week, where he said "I don't care if I ever see him again in my life" and vowed not to travel to Saudi Arabia for a face-off.

Despite voicing his concerns, Fury did say he hopes the next big fight is signed next week and his management confirmed that they are looking to definitely get it done within the next fortnight.

"When the fight is announced, which we anticipate we will do in the next couple of weeks," said Brown. "There's still a couple of contractual things that we need to get through, i.e. where it's going to be, when it's going to be, how it's going to be, but I've been assured that we'll be sorting it out in the next couple of weeks."

Who is the favourite according to the experts?

Former middleweight world title contender Matthew Macklin believes that the 'Gypsy King' is the clear favourite.

"I think Tyson Fury is favourite," said Macklin. "I think because he's got a style and assets that age better. I think AJ is more athletic but as you get older those athletic qualities diminish.

"I think his punch resistance probably has gone now. Dubois, it was a bad knockout, and he's had that fight against Jake Paul since.

"I don't think his punch resistance will be anywhere near what it once was, and also his reflexes won't be what they were, so it's like a double whammy.

"Fury, his reflexes won't be what they were either so it's not like it's all AJ on the decline. He's not the fighter he was. Neither of them were, but I think we all know that and accept that.

"It's still a level playing field because they're both past their best, so it's still going to be an intriguing battle."

As for Sky Sports Boxing expert and former WBO Cruiserweight champion Johnny Nelson , he said: "There's a word called 'mercurial' and that describes Anthony Joshua.

"He's got so much talent but it's a case of which version of him turns up on performance night.

"The talented fighter we know, he wasn't there [on Saturday]. The guts, the heart, he was there, because after 20 seconds he got put down and had to get back up again. He was still making rookie mistakes. I'm thinking, you shouldn't make those mistakes at this stage in your career.

"Listen, I'm an AJ fan, but I'd have to lean towards Tyson Fury's fluidity, his boxing ability – because of that vulnerability from Anthony Joshua, getting caught by that sneaky little uppercut on the inside, getting caught again.

"These are natural shots from Tyson Fury. When it comes to heart, determination, desire and want, I put that in the corner of Anthony Joshua.

"But on last night's performance and on Friday night's performance, I'd have to lean towards Tyson Fury, from what I've seen."

The date and venue announcement is the key piece of outstanding information but, given the November window, that confirmation is expected within weeks.

For reference, tickets for Joshua's fight with Dubois went on sale a little under three months before that event.

The plan once both men came through the weekend was a joint press conference to formally announce the fight, though Fury's refusal to share a stage with Joshua makes the shape of that uncertain and there is also the venue conundrum to answer.

Fury expects a signing within days before fans can look forward to what will be one of the most eagerly awaited British boxing matches of all time.

articles.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua excites me more than ever and Fury has the edge, says Johnny Nelson
articles.summary: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are on course to meet in November after weekend wins over Mariusz Wach and Kristian Prenga; former world champion and Sky Sports boxing expert Johnny Nelson assesses where both men are and names his early favourite
articles.body:
Listen, I'm an AJ fan, but it comes down to what we saw this weekend.

The shots that caught Joshua on Saturday, that sneaky little uppercut on the inside, the one that caught him again, those are natural shots for Tyson Fury.

Heart, determination, desire and want, I put all of that in Joshua's corner. But on Saturday's performance, and on Friday's, it's Fury for me.

And believe me, it takes something for me to say that, because if I'm honest with you, I never thought we'd see Anthony Joshua in the ring again.

I thought it would take him so long to get over what happened emotionally, mentally, spiritually. I think being in the ring, being in the gym training, is probably what has kept him on the path of trying to get himself right again.

Watching him on Saturday, you could still see it bubbling over the top, still see a guy struggling to come to terms with something most people will never experience. It put a lump in my throat.

Just to get in the ring alone was an amazing feat and hats off to him for that.

Then the first round happened, and I thought what most people thought, "he's gone, his punch resistance has gone".

But then it was a case of "Oh my goodness, this fight is going to be so exciting".

He was hit, he was hurt, he looked vulnerable. Nigel Benn looked vulnerable too and he was a dangerous fighter every time he got in a ring.

Joshua is not the fighter he was, but that vulnerability is exactly what will make the Fury fight such compelling viewing.

Are both fighters ready to face each other?

The risk is clear if they don't fight each other soon; look at Saturday night. So it has to be their next fight.

Prenga has a knockout record - he can hit and he can hurt – but he shouldn't have been in Anthony Joshua's league, point blank.

There's a word for AJ, though... mercurial.

He has so much talent but it's a case of which version of Anthony Joshua turns up.

The talented fighter we know wasn't there in Jeddah. The guts and the heart were, because after 20 seconds he was down and had to get back up again.

But he was still making rookie mistakes, and you just shouldn't be making those mistakes at this stage of your career.

You've got to give him a pass, though, because remember what he's coming from.

Boxing for him isn't about the money. I think it's about creating some kind of stability inside himself.

They were boys when this started and they're men now. They've had the losses and they've had the highs, and they need each other to bring the best out of each other.

That's why, even with both men past their best, it's even more exciting now.

The fight won't begin when the first bell goes. It begins in the build-up, in the gamesmanship, in how one fighter gets into the head of the other.

Of course it has to take place in the UK, I just don't think it will.

They can make as much noise as they want, and we want it here. I think this is going stateside because that's where the audience is and that's where the paymaster realistically wants it as well.

Imagine being a fan in November at Wembley, up in the tier seats, freezing cold, waiting for a 2am first bell. I understand historically it should be here but I personally think it'll end up in America.

Either way, this fight is five years behind. We've always wanted to see it, so whatever we get from both fighters, we're going to make the most of it.

articles.title: Zuffa Boxing: Edgar Berlanga climbs off canvas to beat Steven Buttler in Madison Square Garden thriller
articles.summary: Edgar Berlanga stops Steven Butler in New York before calling out Hamzah Sheeraz for rematch; Richardson Hitchins calls out welterweight division after outclassing Ricardo Salas; Callum Walsh fights Tyler Denny on August 8 live on Sky Sports as part of Zuffa Boxing 10
articles.body:
A year on from his knockout defeat to Britain's Hamzah Sheeraz, Berlanga was staring another loss in the face when he was dropped by Butler in the closing seconds of round two.

The knockdown lit the touchpaper, with Berlanga battering Butler around the ring with a succession of heavy shots and forcing his opponent to survive the onslaught by any means necessary.

Butler even launched an MMA-style takedown in an attempt to combat Berlanga, but had his most productive spell when he landed two big shots of his own as the bell sounded to end round three.

The back-and-forth action continued, with Berlanga landing the cleaner and heavier shots before finishing round six with a barrage of right hands that eventually knocked Butler to the canvas.

Butler landed a big right hand at the start of the seventh to offer some resistance, only for matters to be taken out of his hands when Berlanga's devastating combination left the referee with no choice but to stop the fight.

Berlanga's 24th career victory extended his unbeaten record at Madison Square Garden to 6-0 as he set his sights on the biggest names in the super-middleweight division, including a potential shot at avenging his defeat to Sheeraz.

"It shows I'm a true champion, and I'm not sacred of fighting anyone," Berlanga said post-fight. "I fought a dangerous fighter, a big knockout puncher to prove myself and show people I am back.

"We want Hamzah Sheeraz, Jaime Munguia, Chris Eubank, Jermell Charlo, Caleb Plant, we want to fight to best prove we belong with the best."

In the co-main event, former super-lightweight world champion Richardson Hitchins made an emphatic start to life at welterweight, outclassing Ricardo 'Magic Man' Salas in a unanimous decision victory.

Hitchins used his speed, accuracy and reach advantage to dominate throughout, repeatedly snapping Salas back with his jab and rarely allowing the Mexican into the fight.

The one-sided nature of the contest was reflected by three 100-90 scorecards.

Having impressed in his new weight class, Hitchins immediately turned his attention to the division's biggest names, declaring his ambition to face and beat the very best at 147lbs.

"I want the best guys in boxing," Hitchins said. "Give me Gervonta Davis, Devon Haney, Ryan Garcia.

"They say I'm not like that, come show me I'm not like that. 21-0, no draws, no stains on my record. Come get it if you want it."

articles.title: Jessica Barry to fight Reina Tellez on Mikaela Mayer vs Chantelle Cameron undercard on August 29 in Birmingham, live on Sky Sports
articles.summary: Jessica Barry will fight Reina Tellez in Birmingham on August 29; in the main event, Mikaela Mayer takes on Chantelle Cameron for the WBC, WBO and WBA belts at the bp pulse LIVE arena; Caroline Dubois and Tysie Gallagher also feature on the MVP show
articles.body:
The featherweight bout adds to the UK vs USA lineup for MVP Women 06, and represents a significant step up for Barry (10-1-2, 2 KOs) as she faces former junior Olympian Tellez (13-1-1, 5 KOs) not far from her home city of Coventry.

"I turned down three title fights to be on this card, and this opportunity is going to open every door I have been knocking on," said Jessica Barry.

"MVP are leading the way for female boxing and Sky Sports is the platform in the UK. It is now down to me to give a five-star performance."

The contest is her opponent Tellez's first since going the distance in a defeat to unified world champion Amanda Serrano in January, on a card that also features a fight for Caroline Dubois against American Amelia Moore.

"I respect Jessica Barry for accepting the challenge, but when that bell rings, respect gives way to determination. I'm coming to represent the USA with pride, fight with heart, and leave everything in the ring," Tellez, Barry's opponent said.

"I have plenty of time to get ready for this fight, I'll be on another level. Expect fireworks, expect me to be at my best, I'm coming with everything I got."

Joining the preliminary card will be MVP's new signing Tysie Gallagher, with her opponent confirmed as Welsh super-bantamweight Ashleigh Johnson.

Gallagher (10-2) is the current WBO and Commonwealth champion, and is looking to improve her standing as the IBF's No 5 contender in the world.

"MVPW-06 continues to showcase elite matchups representing both the present and future of the UK and USA's storied boxing legacies," said Nakisa Bidarian and Jake Paul, co-founders of Most Valuable Promotions.

"Reina Tellez is a Team USA veteran and proven world championship competitor while Jessica Barry is an English champion, each a perfect fit to join this decorated MVPW-06 UK vs. USA main card of champions and elite contenders.

"Alongside Tysie Gallagher's promotional debut, and another Midlands battle featuring Brandon Bethall, MVPW is back in force on Saturday, August 29, live on Sky Sports."

articles.title: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua could both retire after they finally fight this year, says heavyweight rival Dillian Whyte
articles.summary: Anthony Joshua resumed his career too early says old rival Dillian Whyte after the former world heavyweight champion suffered a massive scare against Kristian Prenga; Joshua was floored twice before stopping Prenga in the second round; Fury and Joshua are set to finally fight in November
articles.body:
Fury and Joshua are expected to finally share the ring in November after they both emerged victorious from their warm-up fights, with America now the likely location for the British heavyweight blockbuster.

But the Brit rivals appear to be in the closing chapters of their careers as Joshua climbed off the canvas twice before stopping Kristian Prenga in the second round, while Fury selected the 46-year-old Mariusz Wach as his opponent before securing a seventh-round stoppage.

Whyte, who has fought both Fury and Joshua, told Sky Sports : "It's hard to say [who will win] because the boxing pugilists will pick Tyson Fury and the hardcore boxing fans will pick Anthony Joshua because AJ's got power and Tyson Fury's feet have slowed down, so I'll say Fury on points [or] AJ by stoppage.

"Potentially, both men could hang up their gloves after the fight. When it's done, they might say, listen, we've done everything, Tyson's won all the belts, AJ's been a unified world champion, they might just say, yeah, that's it.

"I think they might both hang up their gloves after and then it'd be a sad day for boxing."

Joshua returned to the ring for the first time since he was injured in a car crash in December that claimed the lives of his two close friends, Sina Ghami and Latif 'Latz' Ayodele.

After Joshua was floored in the first 20 seconds, Whyte has suggested this was a sign that his old rival was not yet in the right mindset to resume his career.

"Prenga might not have been the best boxer in the world, but he could punch," said Whyte.

"In boxing, anybody can get knocked down. I've been knocked down multiple times in different fights.

"It's kind of hard to say if his punch resistance is gone, you know, I think it's more mental than punch resistance.

"I think he's in a place mentally where he's been through a lot.

"Listen, AJ is not my friend, we don't like each other per se, so you know, I'm just being honest.

"I think it's that it was the nervousness and mentally not being ready for the kind of fight that Prenga brought to him in the early rounds."

Following a loss to Moses Itauma last summer, Whyte is back in training and hopes to sharpen his skills in a comeback bout before targeting a big name.

"I'd love to fight Derek Chisora, Andy Ruiz, Miller," he said. "These are guys from my era that I didn't fight and I'd love to fight them.

"I understand I'm coming off a first-round defeat.

"I'm not deluded - I understand that I need a fight to get myself back into contention, so whoever really.

"I just want to just get a fight back and just get back in the ring, shake some ring rust and just get my groove on again and then fight whoever there is to fight."

articles.title: Caroline Dubois splits from trainer Shane McGuigan ahead of lightweight title defence vs Amelia Moore
articles.summary: Caroline Dubois will take on Amelia Moore in Birmingham on August 29; the event will be headlined by Mikaela Mayer and Chantelle Cameron, who will compete for the unified welterweight world championship; watch MVPW-06 live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
McGuigan, who has established himself as one of the world's best boxing trainers, began working with Dubois in 2021.

The pair have enjoyed some great success together, with McGuigan guiding Dubois to victories over Maira Moneo, Bo Mi Re Shin, and the 25-year-old's unification victory over Terri Harper in April.

Dubois revealed her decision to team up with Manny Robles - the renowned trainer of Andy Ruiz Jr, Oscar Valdez and Brandon Figueroa - was driven solely by her quest to dominate boxing, insisting she had nothing but gratitude for McGuigan.

"Most times fighters leave a coach when they lost, and they want someone to blame or throw under the bus, that's a lame move," Dubois said.

"At the end of the day, I'm so happy and proud of the journey we had had together. I've become the unified world champion, I've announced myself into women's boxing and the biggest stage possible and we did that with Shane McGuigan as my coach and as a massive part of my team.

"I just want to say a massive thank you to Shane McGuigan who was a phenomenal coach and is a phenomenal coach. I'm honoured, proud and privileged to be part of that

"That work doesn't get forgotten, lost or disappear; it grows and adds to the stable. I'm on a quest for greatness and will do whatever it takes to get there, and for me, moving to America and trying a different coaching team is a part of that quest.

"I want to grow and develop and be the best fighter you've ever seen. A fighter should never stop learning or growing or limit themselves."

Dubois and Moore will fight at 135lbs over 10 two-minute rounds at the bp pulse LIVE Arena, with Mikaela Mayer and Chantelle Cameron set to headline the event, which is entirely composed of bouts between UK and USA female fighters.

But the English fighter is "frustrated" by having to defend her titles , rather than unify the belts. She had sought out a fight with Elif Nur Turhan.

"From what I hear and from what my promotors and team are telling me, she [Turhan] asked for such an astronomical, ridiculous amount. It was absurd. It was crazy," Dubois said .

"The amount she asked for, it wasn't even a laugh out of the room. It was just so ridiculous. If I told you, you would think I'm lying.

"So she just isn't about it. She's a joker and what you do with jokers, you just leave them alone. That's retirement money. That's never-fight-again type of money."

Dubois believes the fight with Turhan will happen eventually but is also eyeing up a meeting with WBA lightweight title holder Stephanie Han.

Earlier this year, the British fighter also called out Alycia Baumgardner , saying their much-anticipated bout "has to happen sooner rather than later".

In 2023, McGuigan backed Dubois to "capture all of the belts" , declaring her "the best lightweight in the world".

"Even though the lightweight division is probably the most highly contested division in female boxing, she's blitzing everybody," he told Sky Sports .

McGuigan also said he expected the 25-year-old to become an undisputed champion across multiple weight classes.

"I genuinely believe she can do it at lightweight, super-lightweight and welterweight. She's still developing. She's getting much better all the time."

Scotney: Sometimes you have to make a change

Former undisputed world champion Ellie Scotney told Sky Sports:

"Caroline is a generational talent and I think she's just scratching the surface.

"It's one of those where she has to follow if there's something new that she wants to align.

"Nothing was going wrong for her to make that move. But sometimes you just have to make a change, and I think she's at that place."

articles.title: Skye Nicolson joins Most Valuable Promotions and will defend world title on Mikaela Mayer vs Chantelle Cameron show
articles.summary: Skye Nicolson will make her MVP debut in a 10-round WBC super-bantamweight title defence against Japan’s two-division champion Miyo Yoshida on Mikaela Mayer vs Chantelle Cameron bill; watch MVPW-06: UK vs USA live on Sky Sports on August 29
articles.body:
The 30-year-old Australian will defend her WBC super-bantamweight title against Japan's Miyo Yoshida in her MVP debut on the Mikaela Mayer vs Chantelle Cameron undercard in Birmingham on August 29, live on Sky Sports.

Nicolson, an Olympian who won Commonwealth Games gold in 2018, is the latest high-profile female boxer to join YouTuber Jake Paul's promotional organisation.

"Women's boxing is entering a new era, and I want to be right at the centre of it," said Nicolson.

"My goal has always been to test myself against the very best and be involved in the biggest fights in women's boxing.

"I truly believe this move puts me in the best possible position to do exactly that. I'm excited for what's ahead and can't wait for this next chapter of my career to unfold."

Nicolson (16-1, 3 KOs) faces three-time, two-division world champion Yoshida (19-5, 1 KO), searching for a fifth successive victory as she takes another step towards unifying the super-bantamweight division.

"Skye is one of the most recognisable athletes in women's boxing today," Paul and Nakisa Bidarian, co-founders of Most Valuable Promotions, said.

"As a two-division world champion, Commonwealth Games gold medallist, Olympian and one of Australia's biggest stars, she represents the calibre of athlete we're building MVP around."

The August 29 show at bp pulse LIVE in Birmingham will also see Britain's Caroline Dubois defend her WBC and WBO lightweight titles against Amelia Moore on a card made up entirely of bouts between UK and USA female fighters.

articles.title: Mikaela Mayer declares Chantelle Cameron unification bout in Birmingham will be 'the female fight of the year'
articles.summary: Mikaela Mayer vs Chantelle Cameron will headline MVPW-06 at the bp pulse LIVE arena in Birmingham; WBO, WBA and WBC super welterweight titles on the line in UK vs USA main event; watch MVPW-06: UK vs USA live on Sky Sports on August 29
articles.body:
British world champion Cameron (22-1, 8 KOs) faces American Mayer (22-2, 5 KOs) at the bp pulse LIVE arena in Birmingham on August 29 - live on Sky Sports - with every bout on the MVPW-06 main card pitting a UK fighter against a US opponent.

Unified WBC and WBO lightweight world champion Caroline Dubois and three-weight world champion Terri Harper also feature on the card, but Mayer believes she and Cameron will deliver a main-event fight for the ages with all three world titles on the line in their 10-round contest.

"We know how great this fight is because we made it," Mayer said at the MVPW-06 press conference. "It's a fight we've both always wanted, a fight that will help grow and develop women's boxing, a fight that we need.

"We've both had amazing careers as pros and amateurs. We're older and wiser now, and we know what works and what doesn't for us," the 36 year old added.

"We're at a very similar stage in our careers and are getting each other in our primes. We're both still very strong and dominant, so there is just no way this won't be an action-packed fight.

"I'm predicting the female fight of the year, 100 per cent. I don't see anyone else who can top this.

"Considering our styles, there is no avoiding [standing and trading]. We like to come forward and let our hands go, but we're smart enough to know we can't bang it out the whole time. There will be a lot more high-level boxing than that."

Mayer said she was gearing up to reach a new level of performance, adding: "I'm confident in myself. I'm not going to make it close - I'm that confident in my skills right now.

"People think you cannot get better at this age, that you plateau or that you're as good as you're going to get, but that is not the case with me.

"I've made a lot of changes in my camp, brought fresh eyes in, and I'm getting better, stronger and smarter every day. I feel better now than when I was 26. I'm excited to go out there and show you another level."

Mayer's two career defeats - to Alycia Baumgardner in 2022 and Natasha Jonas in 2024 - came on British soil but her affinity with the UK remains unwavered.

"I won't let things that happened in the past scar me or make me fearful of taking on big challenges in the future," she said.

"I've always loved the UK crowd. I'm like an adopted Brit, I'm 73 per cent British. Every single time I fought in the UK the energy has been unmatched. You're energetic, that pumps me up."

The 35-year-old Cameron won the WBO super welterweight title - a belt Mayer had vacated just months after beating Mary Spencer for it - with a dominant victory over Michaela Kotaskova in April.

Now Mayer is looking to reclaim the belt and unify the division alongside her WBA and WBC titles, but Cameron believes she is more than capable of rising to the challenge.

Asked why she was backing herself to come out on top, Cameron said: "My mindset. I'm a different breed. The tougher the challenge, the better I am.

"I know Mikaela is a tough test, but that will bring the best out of me. I shine when I have opponents like that in front of me. I think I'm unstoppable."

articles.title: Joe Cordina pleads not guilty to charges of assault by beating as former world champion denied US visa for Abdullah Mason fight
articles.summary: Joe Cordina was set to fight Abdullah Mason in the United States on July 4 but his visa application was refused; he was charged with assault in June but has pleaded not guilty
articles.body:
Cordina, 34, a two-time IBF super-featherweight champion, appeared at Cardiff Magistrates' Court on Tuesday and pleaded not guilty to two charges of assault by beating .

South Wales Police previously said the charges relate to an incident outside Pentwyn Service Station in Cardiff on February 27 this year.

During the brief hearing, Cordina appeared in the dock alongside Jamie O'Brien, 32, from Pentwyn, who has also been charged with assault in connection with the incident.

The court previously heard the offences the two men are charged with are alleged to be "against each other".

On Tuesday, Nadeem Majid, representing Cordina, said the second charge of assault he faces "emanates from one continued incident".

O'Brien did not enter a plea during the hearing.

District Judge Charlotte Murphy set a trial date for Cordina of October 13.

She said: "You've pleaded not guilty to two offences, which means there's going to be a trial.

"Until then, I grant you unconditional bail."

Cordina was due to fight for the WBO lightweight title against Abdullah Mason in the United States on July 4, however, his application for a US visa was refused.

articles.title: Jake Paul provided tougher test to Anthony Joshua than Kristian Prenga, says MVP's Nakisa Bidarian
articles.summary: MVP CEO claims Jake Paul gave Anthony Joshua a tougher test than Kristian Prenga and says YouTuber will return to boxing, outlining lengthy shortlist of would-be opponents; watch MVPW-06: UK vs USA live on Sky Sports on August 29
articles.body:
In his first fight since facing YouTuber-turned-boxer Paul last December, Joshua was sent to the canvas by two first-round knockdowns from the unfancied Albanian.

Joshua clawed himself off the canvas twice, eventually knocking Prenga out in emphatic fashion in round two to stay on track for an end-of-year showdown with Tyson Fury.

But as far as Bidarian is concerned, the contest further highlighted how well Paul performed against Joshua over six rounds before the British heavyweight landed a knockout punch that broke his jaw.

"Jake Paul won more than the guy on Saturday night won," Bidarian told Sky Sports News. "He was in there for six rounds. That dude was out in two rounds, taking the same shots Jake was taking.

"I'm very happy with his performance, not happy with the outcome, and didn't like that he broke his jaw, but the hardest shots on Jake Paul didn't do what they did to a heavyweight on Saturday."

Joshua set foot back in the ring for the first time since he survived a fatal car crash that killed two of his friends in Nigeria.

Bidarian expressed his respect and admiration for Joshua, who dedicated the Prenga win to his friends Sina Ghami and Latif 'Latz' Ayodele.

"I'm proud of him, in awe of him, thinking of him," Bidarian said. "I sent him messages throughout the week.

"We developed a relationship with Sina, which was hard for all of us, but no harder for anyone than their families and AJ, who is part of their family.

"For him to make that walk seven months later, to go into the ring with that emotion, I'm sure that weighed heavily on him. Massive respect, massive admiration."

Paul hasn't been seen in the ring since having his jaw broken in two places by Joshua, but Bidarian is adamant his boxing career is anything but over.

The MVP CEO outlined a lengthy shortlist of would-be opponents for Paul, which included former UFC star Francis Ngannou, Britain's Chris Eubank Jr and WBC welterweight world champion Ryan Garcia.

"100 per cent he's boxing again," Bidarian declared.

"Jake wants to fight Ngannou, Ryan Garcia, but Tommy Fury is a fight that makes sense. Edgar Berlanga, that's a fascinating fight. I also like Chris Eubank Jr, that's a fascinating fight.

"The fighters on the other side also need to be realistic. Sometimes their eyes are bigger than what the box office affords us to pay."

articles.title: Kayla Allen: Decorated British amateur becomes first female fighter to sign with Zuffa Boxing ahead of September pro debut
articles.summary: Kayla Allen will make her professional debut live on Sky Sports on September 26, on the undercard of ZUFFA BOXING 11, headlined by British heavyweight star Johnny Fisher
articles.body:
The 21-year-old Londoner will campaign as a lightweight and make her first professional appearance on September 26, live on Sky Sports, at the Copper Box Arena on the undercard of ZUFFA BOXING 11, headlined by heavyweight star Johnny Fisher.

Allen's deal with Zuffa Boxing marks the latest step in a remarkable rise to a boxing career that began when she first put on a pair of gloves less than five years ago.

"I'm delighted to have signed with Zuffa Boxing as their first female athlete," Allen said.

"I feel honoured to be in this position. With the backing of Zuffa and Sky Sports, I can become a big star on both sides of the Atlantic.

"I appreciate my team for believing in me and securing this landmark deal. I'll be bringing the heat in the ring, and my fans will bring the noise on September 26."

Allen's ascent to becoming one of Britain's most accomplished young amateurs started when she set up a heavy bag in her garden and began learning the craft by watching videos of Floyd Mayweather Jr. and Mike Tyson.

After a short stint on the white-collar circuit, Allen joined GB Boxing and reached the Senior Elite finals in her first year as an amateur.

She captured gold at many of Europe's most prestigious tournaments, including the 2024 Haringey Box Cup and the 2025 Senior Elite Championships.

Allen concluded her amateur career with triumphs at the 2025 European U23 Championships and 2026 Boxam Tournament in La Nucia, Spain. She will begin her professional career under the guidance of long-time trainer Alex Leo.

articles.title: Moses Itauma can become the new IBF world heavyweight champion when he fights Filip Hrgovic on August 29
articles.summary: Moses Itauma could be crowned as the new IBF world heavyweight champion in next fight against Filip Hrgovic; The 21-year-old can claim the vacant IBF title in clash with Hrgovic at The O2 on August 29; IBF no 1 contender Frank Sanchez guaranteed a fight against Itauma vs Hrgovic winner
articles.body:
Oleksandr Usyk announced his decision to vacate the WBC, WBA and IBF belts last month and the unbeaten British contender now has the opportunity to become the new IBF world champion in his clash with Croatian Hrgovic at The O2.

Frank Sanchez, who is the IBF No 1 contender after his knockout victory over Richard Torrez Jnr in May, has been guaranteed a shot at the Itauma vs Hrgovic winner.

Itauma has blazed his path to a world title shot with 14 victories, featuring 12 knockouts, and he ruthlessly stopped Jermaine Franklin in Manchester in March.

But the 21-year-old is taking a sizeable step up in class against Hrgovic, who holds victories over Zhilei Zhang and Joe Joyce, with his only loss coming against Daniel Dubois by stoppage in 2024.

Cuban Sanchez will lie in wait for the new IBF champion, having secured a mandatory shot at the IBF belt after his explosive second-round stoppage of Torrez Jr.

Sanchez's manager Mike Borao said: "Frank Sanchez has allowed Itauma and Hrgovic to fight for the vacant IBF title on August 29 under the condition, as mandatory #1 contender, he fights the winner with no intervening bouts.

"Frank didn't want to fight until the end of the year in order to prepare properly, so the timeline works perfectly for him, especially considering the Itauma vs Hrgovic fight is less than 30 days away.

"The deal we negotiated for Frank to fight the winner is lucrative financially, he maintains his mandatory status, and is only deferring his opportunity a few months.

"The agreement was relatively easy to make with Queensberry and Warriors Boxing, although at times it looked like a deal would fail to materialize.

"I've known George Warren a long time. He understands the heavyweight division, is a gentleman and pleasure to work with. The final deal is good for the participating boxers, promoters, the IBF, and the fans. I am glad it got over the finish line.

"Frank is anxious to fight Ituama or Hrgovic, he doesn't care who it is, and wishes the best of luck to both. He feels he will beat either and become heavyweight champion this year, the target date being December."

The IBF belt is the last remaining vacant title as Agit Kabayel has been elevated as the new WBC champion, while Murat Gassiev has been upgraded to WBA champion.

articles.title: Aaron McKenna to target Chris Eubank Jr and more after dream world title fight against Etinosa Oliha on Saturday
articles.summary: "20 years I've been boxing and it's all going to come down to this night." Aaron McKenna fights Etinosa Oliha for the IBF middleweight world championship in Dublin on Saturday, live on Sky Sports; McKenna believes victory could lead him to Chris Eubank Jr and more
articles.body:
Ireland's McKenna gets his dream world title fight on Saturday, live on Sky Sports , when he boxes Etinosa Oliha for the IBF championship at the 3Arena in Dublin.

"It's something I've been dreaming of since I started boxing at six years old. Finally to get a fight for the world title and for it to be in Ireland makes it extra special," McKenna told Sky Sports .

"I have goosebumps just thinking about fighting in there with that Irish atmosphere.

"20 years I've been boxing and it's all going to come down to this night."

McKenna believes victory would put him in the frame for more high profile fights.

"I want to become undisputed and then become a multiple weight world champion. I'm 6ft 2, I can go all the way to heavyweight with my size! By the time my career's over I'll be fighting at heavyweight! That said, I want to clean up the middleweight division because it definitely is there to be cleaned up and just have the biggest fights possible," he said.

He would welcome a fight with Chris Eubank Jr. The Brighton star, the son of British legend Chris Eubank, last boxed at middleweight and is expected to return at 168lbs. McKenna is convinced it could happen.

"Try and get a win for the Eubank name [in Ireland]," McKenna urged. "You had Eubank [Senior] and Steve Collins, they fought in Cork on Sky Sports . So you never know. If he wants to run a similar story back we can do it in Ireland on Sky Sports again, just recreate history.

"After this show on August 8, Irish boxing will have a big star and it's going to bring massive, massive headlines and a new audience to Irish boxing."

He knows though that Oliha harbours his own ambitions. "He's a very good fighter, strong, he'll be game and any man that's fighting for world titles is going to be giving it their all," McKenna said.

His faith in himself though is total. "I know what I have to do," he added. "I'm more than ready for it.

"The main goal has always been the world title since I started boxing and I've always believed I would become world champion. So on August 8 becoming world champion will definitely open a lot of doors for me."

articles.title: Callum Walsh: From working on fishing boats to ferocious sparring at the Wild Card gym - the making of a fighter
articles.summary: Callum Walsh doesn't back down from danger; he's gone from working on fishing boats to forging a stellar amateur career, proving himself at the famous Wild Card gym and insists he's ready for anybody in the sport; Walsh fights Tyler Denny on Saturday live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
On Saturday, live on Sky Sports , he fights former European champion Tyler Denny at the 3Arena in Dublin.

It will be a test for Walsh against a dangerous opponent, one that he welcomes.

"I'm ready for anybody. I love to challenge myself. I love to fight," Walsh told Sky Sports .

The Irishman is returning to the 3Arena for his first fight in Dublin since knocking out Przemyslaw Runowski in two rounds in 2024.

"It was one of the best nights of my life. Walking out in front of that crowd was insane," the 25-year-old said. "It looks like there was 20,000 people there and it felt like there was 20,000 people there.

"It was crazy. I can't even describe it."

He's come a long way from working on fishing boats as a teenager in Cork. That was a demanding profession with its own kind of dangers.

"I got this fishing job just randomly, I didn't want to work anywhere inside," Walsh remembered.

"It was seven days a week, it was hard work, it wasn't easy but the best job ever in the summer, when it's sunny and you can jump off the boat and swim. You start at four o'clock in the morning. It was very hard [work].

He'd haul crab and lobster pots on deck, rebait them and send them back to pulled down by their anchor.

"If you stack them in the wrong order, you're [in trouble]. The whole boat is going to go. Crazy. It's dangerous work," Walsh explained.

"If they're in the wrong order you're going to have rope all over the place, there's going to be stuff flying. You're going to get tangled up, you're going to get dragged overboard, dragged down with them. Even if it's four or five o'clock in the morning you have to be switched on.

"[One time] I put them back in the wrong order, my leg got trapped on the side of the boat between the rope and the boat, but we were able to get the boat in reverse quick and I was able to get my leg out. Stuff like that is very dangerous if you don't know what you're doing."

All the while he was pursuing a highly decorated amateur career which saw him winning medals domestically and on the international scene.

But he chose to pursue professional boxing and found his way to Freddie Roach's famous Wild Card gym in LA. He had to prove himself straightaway. Roach threw the youngster into sparring on his first day.

"If you want to train here, you have to spar.' He [Roach] wanted to see if I was even worth being there. I sparred the first day and he told me to come back again tomorrow," Walsh said.

"I was in there sparring everybody and anyone for a year and then I made my pro debut.

"Someone will come in [to the Wild Card] for sparring, you know that they're not really supposed to be there," Walsh continued.

"Freddie would tell you: 'Show this guy he's not supposed to be here.' I've knocked so many people out in that gym, I've seen so many people not come back. That's how it is. Freddie Roach's gym is known for being one of the best gyms in the world, known for tough sparring and Freddie he takes pride in that."

His experiences in California helped forge the fighter Walsh is today. "Coming from a massive amateur background, to learning the pro style and how aggressive his pro style is. I think it's the perfect combination," Walsh said.

"Being able to go over to Freddie and learn that aggressive pro style from someone who's had so much experience, I think it's the perfect mixture"

He is determined to show what he can do against Denny on Saturday. "I just believe in my own ability. I just believe if I've trained and prepared to my best I can beat anybody."

articles.title: Joseph Parker says he will return to ring 'soon' after drugs ban lifted following failed test last October
articles.summary: Joseph Parker says he will be back in the ring 'soon'; traces of cocaine were discovered in a routine test given to the UK Anti-Doping Agency on the day of his defeat to Britain's Fabio Wardley in October
articles.body:
The heavyweight's routine test given to UK Anti-Doping on the day of his defeat by Fabio Wardley last October returned traces of cocaine following the loss by 11th-round stoppage at The O2.

Parker, who denied taking any banned substances, could have faced up to a two-year ban from boxing.

However, he has now released a statement saying his suspension has been lifted.

General Secretary of the British Boxing Board of Control, Robert Smith declined to comment when contacted by Sky Sports News but confirmed the suspension has been lifted.

"I'm pleased to confirm my provisional suspension is lifted and I'll be back in the ring soon. I've been advised to say no more for now while details are finalised. Thank you to all my supporters," Parker said on Wednesday.

Parker, 34, is a former world champion who lost his belt to Anthony Joshua in 2018, but he went into his fight against Wardley in arguably the best form of his career.

After a punishing loss to Joe Joyce in 2022, Parker won his next six contests prior, picking up statement wins over Deontay Wilder and Zhilei Zhang, as well as winning the WBO Interim strap.

He was due to challenge then-IBF belt-holder Daniel Dubois in February, only for Dubois to fall ill just days before the fight was meant to take place.

Parker put his position as the WBO mandatory challenger to undisputed champion Oleksandr Usyk on the line by taking the fight against Wardley, but it was a gamble that backfired.

articles.title: Raven Chapman: Boxer undergoes emergency surgery after collapsing following sparring session in Denmark
articles.summary: Boxer Raven Chapman remains in hospital after collapsing following a sparring session in Denmark; she suffered a bleed on the brain and was rushed to hospital and underwent emergency surgery; Chapman fought Skye Nicolson for the WBC world featherweight title back in 2024
articles.body:
During training, Chapman collapsed and was rushed to hospital on July 24 where she was placed in a medically induced coma. A GoFundMe has been launched, with Chapman's team hoping she can return to the UK under medical supervision.

The statement from her management team read: "On Friday, July 24, Raven unexpectedly collapsed after a sparring session in Denmark. Emergency services were called immediately, and she was airlifted to a local hospital. She was diagnosed with a brain haematoma and cerebral oedema.

"Raven underwent emergency surgery immediately. The procedure successfully stopped the bleeding and helped stabilise the swelling. She was then placed in a medically induced coma. Over the past day, she has been taken off the sedatives and is continuing to receive treatment while awaiting medically supervised repatriation to a hospital in the UK, where her rehabilitation is expected to take some time.

"Her doctors are doing everything they can to support her recovery, and we remain hopeful as she continues to fight through this incredibly difficult time. Raven's family are in Denmark supporting her during this incredibly difficult time. We kindly ask that their privacy is respected.

"At this stage, this is the only update we are able to provide. If there are any significant developments, we will share further information when it is appropriate to do so. Thank you for your continued support. Please keep Raven and her loved ones in your thoughts during this challenging time."

Back in 2024, Chapman challenged Skye Nicolson for the WBC world featherweight title, with Nicolson winning by unanimous decision.

Nicolson commented on the post from Chapman's management with: "Praying for a speedy recovery. Can't believe this. Hearts broken for you champ. Keep fighting."

Founder of Queensberry Promotions Frank Warren, who used to manage Chapman, released a statement on social media on Wednesday, saying: "Raven is fully in my thoughts this morning, I'm really hoping she can pull through and get home safely.

"Everyone at Queensberry is behind you Raven, we're all hoping you can pull through this."

articles.title: Joseph Parker 'relieved' after drugs ban was lifted and could target winner of Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley rematch
articles.summary: Joseph Parker denied taking any banned substances after returning traces of cocaine in a Voluntary Anti-Doping Agency test on day of defeat by Fabio Wardley in October; The British Boxing Board of Control confirmed the suspension has been lifted; Parker is set to fight again this year
articles.body:
The New Zealander returned traces of cocaine in a UK Anti-Doping test on the day of his defeat by Fabio Wardley in October, but Parker denied taking any banned substances and the British Boxing Board of Control confirmed the suspension has been lifted.

Parker's manager Higgins is planning the next career move for the former WBO world heavyweight champion, who could fight twice before the end of 2026.

"A combination of relieved, excited, and energised," said Higgins when asked about Parker's current mindset.

"Joseph is champing at the bit to get back into the ring. He was up early to go for a run this morning.

"He feels like he is at the peak of his powers and they say a heavyweight only reaches his prime in his thirties. Joseph is only 34 and if you look at the names on his resume, you could call him a veteran but he's still relatively young.

"Joseph has said to me that he would love to fight this year," Higgins added. "It could be a tune-up, then a big fight at the end of the year or it could be a big fight at the end of the year."

Parker has shared the ring with virtually every top heavyweight of his era, including Anthony Joshua, Deontay Wilder, Andy Ruiz Jr, Derek Chisora, Dillian Whyte, Fabio Wardley, Joe Joyce and Zhilei Zhang.

That 11th-round stoppage loss inflicted by Wardley stopped Parker's charge towards another world title, but Higgins is 'supremely confident' that the Kiwi can become champion again.

"Joseph is confident. He's done it before; he knows what to do. He's going to have another run at the title and is excited to do so.

"He's a free agent so right now we're looking at all offers. We'll look at anything that makes sense. We'll look at its merit on a risk-and-return basis.

"I'm supremely confident that he can become a world champion again. If you look at history, I think even Lennox Lewis copped a couple of losses and then in his 30s it all came together and he was unbeatable.

"We're not quitters and Joseph is looking forward to this final two or three run in his career."

Parker's old WBO belt lies in the hands of Daniel Dubois, who will defend it against Wardley in a rematch later this year.

A fight against the Dubois vs Wardley 2 winner is an option that excites Parker, who would also welcome a rematch with Dillian Whyte.

"If you recall, Joseph had a world title fight against Dubois scheduled and then he mysteriously pulled out a few days before the fight [through illness]," said Higgins.

"Bakole got slotted in; Joseph knocked out Bakole. But there is absolutely unfinished business there with both.

"Joseph is not afraid to get in the ring with anyone. He also has unfinished business with Dillian Whyte and we'd love that rematch.

"If the deal is right and the terms are right, he would love to make any of those fights happen."

articles.title: Aaron McKenna wants to unify the middleweight championships, rise through divisions and then fight at heavyweight!
articles.summary: Aaron McKenna fights Etinosa Oliha for the IBF middleweight world championship at the 3Arena in Dublin, live on Sky Sports; McKenna has an ambitious vision to unify world championships at middleweight before eventually fighting at heavyweight
articles.body:
But his plans do not finish with Etinosa Oliha and the IBF belt this weekend. He wants to "clean up" the division, go undisputed and eventually finish his career as a heavyweight.

It sounds preposterous for an albeit tall, but fairly scrawny 160-pounder. McKenna, though he says it with a smile, sounds serious that this is his long-time vision.

"That's something we talked about a lot, finishing up at heavyweight. I'm six foot three now and I have a very long reach as well. My body's the type of body that could fill out easily enough as well weight-wise," McKenna told Sky Sports .

"Once I'm done at 160lb, take over 168 and then 175. But by the time I finish out, I plan to have at least one fight at heavyweight.

"In the heavyweight division now, sometimes it just takes good footwork and boxing to beat them. It's different from the heavyweights back in the day."

McKenna, it's safe to say, has an eerie confidence in himself. His first task is to become a world champion against a dangerous opponent on Saturday.

"He's a very good fighter, 22-0, strong, he'll be game and any man that's fighting for world titles is going to be giving it their all," McKenna said of Oliha. "I know what I have to do.

"I'm more than ready for it," he added. "It doesn't matter what he brings, whether he comes forward, whether he goes back, I'm ready for everything. I've trained for every style possible my whole life. Whatever he brings, I'm just focused on what I'm doing and what I'm going to do in there."

This, he insists, is the start of a charge through the middleweight division. He wants to take on the other champions. Carlos Adames, the WBC titlist and Denzel Bentley, the new WBO belt-holder, will be in his sights.

"The middleweight division, it's been dying for years now. The last two big fighters in it were Canelo and GGG [Gennady Golovkin], so I kind of want to bring big-time boxing in the middleweight division and bring it back to life," McKenna declared.

"I've done a lot of sparring with [Adames] back in Robert Garcia's gym back in 2019. I was 19 at the time and he was mid-20s. I had no problem with him.

"He doesn't like my style of fighting. When you put it on him, he kind of doesn't like that sort of stuff.

"[Bentley] would be another good fight. He's a world champion now, so if he wants to take the fight, I'd definitely take it because the name of the game is to unify, become the best in the division.

"But all I'm focused on right now is this Saturday. I have a job to do with Oliha and that's becoming world champion and I will become world champion."

McKenna's manager Mike Borao told Sky Sports : "Obviously the focus right now is squarely on this Saturday for Aaron McKenna - he has to get past Etinosa Oliha first before anyone starts mapping out the future.

"That said, Denzel Bentley is a very intriguing possibility. Aaron is the type of fighter who goes out there and delivers for the fans, and few things light up a boxing crowd quite like a proper Ireland vs UK showdown.

"Bentley does have a tough mandatory in Yoenli Hernandez waiting in the wings, though, so it will be interesting to see how things develop.

"In any event, Aaron McKenna has a very exciting future with endless possibilities on Zuffa Boxing."

articles.title: Jake Paul's rematch with Tommy Fury 'makes most sense' as American star plans boxing return, says Nakisa Bidarian
articles.summary: Jake Paul eyes return to boxing by January after sustaining broken jaw in Anthony Joshua loss; Tommy Fury rematch is possible comeback fight; watch Cherneka Johnson vs Dina Thorslund battle for undisputed world titles, live from 3am on Sky Sports this Sunday
articles.body:
Paul has not been seen in the ring since suffering a sixth-round defeat to Anthony Joshua in December 2025, during which he suffered a broken jaw in two places at the hands of the British heavyweight.

The YouTuber-turned-boxer has recovered, rehabilitated and set his sights on a comeback within the next five months.

"In terms of timing, we continue to focus on the end of this year or January. That's the timeline for his return," Bidarian, Paul's partner at MVP, told Sky Sports .

Paul's defeat to Joshua was the second of his 14-fight career, with the only other blemish on his record coming against Fury in 2023, a split decision points loss after the Brit had been floored in the final round.

Victories over former heavyweight world champion Mike Tyson, former middleweight world champion Julio Cesar Chavez Jr and ex-UFC star Nate Diaz have helped Paul earn credibility in the sport, and Bidarian now believes the time is right to avenge his defeat to Fury.

"If we're able to come to terms with Tommy, that's the fight that makes the most sense," he added. "If you think about where they were three years ago, it's the perfect opportunity to show the world that both of them have evolved as boxers.

"For Jake, coming off the loss to AJ, this is his chance to really demonstrate that he has moved to another level, and for Tommy this is his opportunity to say the Jake Paul story has come to an end."

Asked what obstacles stood between Paul and Fury signing a second fight, Bidarian replied: "Money, expectations and the reality of the economics."

Since the Paul victory, Fury has beaten YouTuber KSI on points and also defeated former World's Strongest Man Eddie Hall by majority decision in a Misfits Boxing exhibition bout in June.

articles.title: Joseph Parker: Former heavyweight champion claimed failed drug test was caused by cocaine use of nutritionist ahead of Fabio Wardley fight
articles.summary: Joseph Parker returned an adverse analytical finding for a metabolite of cocaine during a UKAD test shortly after his surprise defeat to Fabio Wardley in London last October; UKAD have revealed Parker claimed the result was caused by exposure to cocaine being used by his nutritionist
articles.body:
Parker returned an adverse analytical finding (AAF) for benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine, during a routine UKAD test shortly after his surprise defeat to Fabio Wardley in London on October 25 last year.

The New Zealander, who has throughout the saga denied taking any prohibited substance, announced on Wednesday that his suspension, which could have lasted as long as two years, had been lifted and that he would be "back in the ring soon".

On Thursday, UKAD officially confirmed Parker was free to resume his career as details of the case were shared, which included the 34-year-old's explanation for the adverse finding.

A UKAD statement said: "On 6 March 2026, Mr Parker provided UKAD with evidence claiming that the AAF was the result of his exposure to cocaine used by the nutritionist he had employed in preparation for the bout on 25 October 2025.

"The nutritionist stated that he was a regular user of cocaine and had used cocaine daily in the week leading up to the bout.

"Between 14 April 2026 and 3 June 2026, UKAD requested further information from Mr Parker in relation to his explanation for the AAF. Amongst other matters, Mr Parker stated that he had first worked with the same nutritionist in April 2023."

UKAD explained that a decision had been made to impose a three-month period of ineligibility, which it already considers served, because an independent scientific expert was satisfied that any ingestion of cocaine had occurred out of competition, and therefore in a context unrelated to sporting performance.

The statement said: "On 15 June 2026, UKAD received an independent scientific expert opinion from its instructed expert, which concluded that Mr Parker's ingestion of cocaine most likely took place out of competition (i.e. before 11:59pm on 24 October 2025).

"On 22 June 2026, UKAD confirmed to Mr Parker that in light of the opinion from its expert, it was satisfied that any ingestion of cocaine occurred out of competition and for that reason would have been in a context unrelated to sport performance.

"Consequently, UKAD lifted Mr Parker's Provisional Suspension on that date (allowing him to resume his participation in sport with immediate effect) and proposed a three-month period of Ineligibility (deemed served) by way of sanction for his Anti-Doping Rule Violation."

The scientific expert believed it possible that Parker's administration of cocaine "may have occurred" from contamination, but also said they could not exclude the possibility the finding had arisen "as the tail end of the administration of a larger pharmacologically active dose of cocaine."

With the UKAD report, the scientific expert said: "It is also my opinion that Mr Parker's administration of cocaine may have occurred orally from food contaminated with cocaine by his sports nutritionist who has admitted being a user of cocaine giving rise to the finding of benzoylecgonine in Mr Parker's urine Samples.

"I cannot exclude the possibility that the finding of benzoylecgonine has arisen as the tail end of the administration of a larger pharmacologically active dose of cocaine."

The result of Parker's bout against Wardley, which was an 11th-round stoppage victory for the Brit, becomes a defeat by disqualification, rather than knockout.

Parker lost his world title to Anthony Joshua in 2018, but went into his fight against Wardley in arguably the best form of his career.

After a punishing loss to Joe Joyce in 2022, Parker won his next six contests prior, picking up statement wins over Deontay Wilder and Zhilei Zhang, as well as winning the WBO Interim strap.

He was due to challenge then-IBF belt-holder Daniel Dubois in February, only for Dubois to fall ill just days before the fight was meant to take place.

Parker put his position as the WBO mandatory challenger to undisputed champion Oleksandr Usyk on the line by taking the fight against Wardley, but it was a gamble that backfired.

articles.title: Fury vs Joshua: Eddie Hearn expects British heavyweight fight to be finalised by end of August despite concerns over location
articles.summary: Eddie Hearn insists Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua will be finalised by the end of August despite concerns over relocating the fight to New York; Hearn asserts that Joshua is keen to fight Fury on British soil
articles.body:
New York has emerged as the most likely venue for Fury vs Joshua, with Madison Square Garden poised to host the two British stars.

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn insists he is yet to agree that the bout can be moved to the States, but still expects the fight to be finalised this month.

"At the end of August, there will be a press conference," Hearn told Sky Sports News.

"I'm not going to sit here and tell you there's no way the fight's happening in America because things can change.

"But I really feel strongly that this is something that should happen in the UK and we'll do all we can.

"We're up against it - it seems like everybody else has agreed but Anthony Joshua. He feels a little bit of responsibility to UK fight fans as well, and he's doing everything he can to give them what they want."

Discussion about a change of venue has led to speculation that the fight could be delayed, but Hearn remains optimistic that an in-shape Anthony Joshua will be ready to fight in November no matter the location.

"We're ready to go in November - so there's no reason for this fight to be delayed," Hearn added.

"We will try and make it as financially unviable as possible to do this fight in the US, so that hopefully they just turn around and say, 'okay, let's just do it in the UK'.

"Apparently, [New York] is the entertainment capital of the world. Who cares? It's two Brits and the biggest fight in the British boxing history. But I understand business."

articles.title: Itauma vs Hrgovic: Can fast-tracked 21-year-old Briton make history on Saturday?
articles.summary: Can heavyweight Moses Itauma become world champion at 21 by beating Filip Hrgovic on Saturday or has the fast-tracked Briton arrived too soon?
articles.body:
British heavyweight Moses Itauma pulls out his phone and scrolls through his pictures.

He shows a meme featuring former Nigerian president Olusegun Obasanjo in traditional attire, standing with his hands on his hips and staring deadpan into the camera.

"This is how an African dad looks at you when you pursue a career that goes against his wishes and you turn out to be successful," a chuckling Itauma reads aloud to BBC Sport. "That is pretty much my dad."

Itauma was born in Slovakia to a Nigerian father and a Slovak mother before moving to Kent as a young child.

His parents originally wanted him to become a doctor or a lawyer. But once his older brother turned professional and the family recognised Itauma's exceptional natural talent, their stance softened.

"Don't worry about school. Just focus on your boxing," his mother eventually said.

That decision has paid off spectacularly.

At 21, Itauma steps into the ring against Filip Hrgovic on Saturday for the vacant IBF title with the chance to become the second-youngest world heavyweight champion in history.

"There's a lot of expectations on my shoulders to carry the flag of British boxing. I just have to live up to it," Itauma says.

Victory against Croatia's Hrgovic would put Itauma on the path to becoming the next big name in British heavyweight boxing, with Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua inching closer to the end of their storied careers.

Fury, with his Netflix documentaries and larger-than-life personality, has always made himself the attraction. Itauma is more like Joshua - guarded and keeping the media at arm's length.

"What irritates me most is when people think you're public property," he says.

"What people don't know about me is that I don't actually want to be in the limelight. The way my career is going, I just have no choice."

Like Joshua, Itauma often appears uninterested in the theatrics of fight week. When Hrgovic interrupted during Thursday's news conference, Itauma calmly asked host Adam Smith for the next question.

There are similarities in their careers, too.

Joshua fought Charles Martin for the IBF title in his 16th pro bout, having boxed 34 rounds. Itauma arrives at his first world-title opportunity a fight sooner and with 31 rounds logged.

While Joshua had an Olympic gold medal and a deeper amateur background, victory for Itauma would make comparisons unavoidable - eclipsing Joshua to become the fastest British heavyweight to win a world title.

Itauma's trainer Ben Davison, who also worked with Joshua and Fury, believes he has the temperament to handle what comes next.

"Moses has already had that pressure for such a long time and I just think it's water off a duck's back."

Should Itauma have been given a title shot?

Boxing's best young prospects tend to be handled carefully and are given time to learn before dangerous tests arrive.

Itauma, however, has been fast-tracked to his world-title shot.

Francis Warren - son of Queensberry chief Frank - first noticed him as a teenager, sparring established professionals. Former British heavyweight champion Jeamie 'TKV' Tshikeva was there even earlier.

"Moses was a big 11 or 12-year-old, around 75 to 80kg, (11st 11lb to 12st 8lb) and sparred an adult of the same weight," TKV says. "He really showed up, put hands on this grown man, and I was shocked.

"The guy he sparred was around 25. Imagine going home and telling your wife you got beat up by a kid."

Itauma's progress has been marked by destructive stoppages over Dillian Whyte and Jermaine Franklin. They may not be world-beaters, but the manner of those wins strengthened belief Itauma was destined for the top.

When Oleksandr Usyk vacated the IBF title and Frank Sanchez agreed to step aside, Itauma's fight with Hrgovic was elevated into a world-title contest.

Suddenly, the fast track looked, to some, like a shortcut.

Hrgovic - even before the IBF belt was on the line - claimed Itauma had been handed "everything on a plate". On social media, there was a similar feeling - perhaps a final eliminator would have been a more natural way to earn his shot.

Itauma, though, has little interest in proving himself to the doubters.

"It's a lose-lose situation for me because if I win, I've done what people expect, and if I lose, it's just like, I wasn't as good as what I thought," he says.

"I don't find happiness in trying to please other people's expectations."

Mike Tyson's mark as the youngest heavyweight champion in history - 20 years, four months and 22 days - remains boxing's ultimate holy grail.

While that record has passed, victory over Hrgovic would make Itauma the second-youngest heavyweight champion ever and boxing's youngest active world champion.

The Chatham heavyweight has never fought 12 rounds. He has never even sparred 12.

"Although I haven't gone 12 rounds and I haven't taken one on the chin, I don't think that's a characteristic you need to become a heavyweight champion," he says.

But what happens when his power does not end the fight? What happens when an opponent is still standing in round eight, still dangerous, still coming back?

TKV, who has sparred Joshua, Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley, has seen enough behind closed doors to believe Itauma can handle it.

"Moses works hard even though he hasn't had to face adversity in his fights or training," he says. "I've never seen him slack. He's fast, sharp, a good learner and I rarely see him get hit.

"I believe he can do the rounds, too. He has the potential to dominate the division for years."

There is no doubt within Itauma's camp that he belongs at this level. But all the outside questions over timing, merit and readiness will fade when the first bell sounds.

On Saturday, the prodigy has 12 rounds - if he needs them - to write his own chapter in heavyweight history.
