articles.summary: UFC Shanghai results, highlights, live discussion and instant play-by-play, reactions and analysis.
articles.body:
Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) is live THIS MORNING (Sat., Aug. 29, 2026) with UFC Shanghai , streaming live online via Paramount+ . The event happens at Shanghai Oriental Sports Center in Shanghai, China. The main event is Umar Nurmagomedov vs. Song Yadong in the Bantamweight division.

The UFC returns to China for the second time this year. In May they were in Macau. And this is also the second time they've been to Shanghai in as many years. Who can forget the massive upset Johnny Walker pulled off over The Mountain Tiger the last time they were here?

There's a home soil hero on this card, too. It's Song Yadong . But it will be an upset if he manages to pull off the win against the -600 Umar Nurmagomedov . Nurmagomedov will be looking for a suffocating victory to get himself back in the title picture against fellow countryman Petr Yan .

The co-main event is Yan Xiaonan vs. Denise Gomes . Former title challenger Yan is climbing past her mid-thirties, but she will hope she has enough left in the tank to beat the rising Brazilian talent. Gomes will have revenge on her mind in this fight. Yan once knocked out Gomes' mentor Jessica Andrade .

Rounding out the main card is Aoriqileng vs. Kai Asakura , Alex Perez vs. Sumudaerji , Liu Ce vs. Levi Rodrigues Jr. and Bilal Hasan vs. Nilson Rojas . A number of those fights seem engineered to produce viral moments.

The features 'Prelim' is Namsrai Batbayar vs. Andre Lima at Flyweight. Lima missed weight for this one . The undercard also has Rei Tsuruya vs. Kevin Borjas , Jack Jenkins vs. Sean Woodson , Xiao Long vs. Francesco Nuzzi , Lawrence Lui vs. Hector Santiago , Jingnan Xiong vs. Julia Polastri and Ding Meng vs. Cam Nelson.

We are operating at prime local time today. That means it is an extremely early wake up for me and anyone else on the east coast. Check out these special air times below:

UFC Shanghai "Prelims" will begin at 3 a.m. ET .

UFC Shanghai main card is scheduled to start at 6 a.m. ET .

All of UFC Shanghai airs on Paramount+ , which you can stream here .

The live blog here starts rolling below at 3 a.m. ET . Come in and say hi!

135 lbs.: Umar Nurmagomedov vs. Song Yadong

205 lbs.: Liu Ce def. Levi Rodrigues by KO (right hook), round 1 (4:26)

125 lbs.: Bilal Hasan def. Nilson Rojas by KO (straight right), round 2 (2:28)

125 lbs.: Andre Lima def. Namsrai Batbayar by submission (guillotine), round 3 (3:03)

125 lbs.: Rei Tsuruya def. Kevin Borjas by submission (rear naked choke), round 1 (4:14)

145 lbs.: Sean Woodson def. Jack Jenkins by split decision (29-28, 28-29, 29-28)

135 lbs.: Francesco Nuzzi def. Xiao Long by TKO (punches), round 1 (1:00)

135 lbs.: Hector Santiago def. Lawrence Lui by KO (punches), round 2 (0:53)

115 lbs.: Julia Polastri def. Jingnan Xiong by KO (headkick), round 1 (3:06)

170 lbs.: Cam Nelson def. Ding Meng by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-28)

Round 1: Ce bounces around like a karate fighter. He's much bigger than Rodrigues. Rodrigues lands the first hard shot, though. That has Ce covering up, but he's fine. Rodrigues is a lot more willing to engage at this point. He lands a hard one-two. Ce is just offering leg kicks, but those aren't keeping Rodrigues away from him. Rodrigues catches a kick and puts Ce on the fence. Now they brawl. I think Ce senses some urgency here. He pops Rodrigues' head back with some nice jabs. He then drops Rodrigues with a hook. Rodrigues is up, but he's wobbly. Ce is slow to realize. He misses on a spinning kick. Now he lands some hard punches. Rodrigues covers up on the fence. Ce pours it on, but Rodrigues stays in there. He fires back and gets off the fence. Ce hurts him again and Rodrigues is back on the fence. Rodrigues lands another hard shot, but Ce responds and sleeps Rodrigues! What a round/fight!

Official decision: Liu Ce def. Levi Rodrigues by KO (right hook), round 1 (4:26)

Round 1: Hasan looks very lively early on. He looks so much faster than Rojas. He lands a nice body kick that has Rojas hurt. Hasan doesn't rush, though. Rojas is able to recover. Hasan gets a takedown and lands some good ground and pound. Rojas works back to his feet, but catches a knee on the way up. Hasan lands more combos to finish a strong round.

Round 2: Rojas rocks Hasan early with a big punch! Hasan is able to recover quickly, though. Rojas is too tired to really push and capitalize anyway. Moments later Hasan steps in and lands a straight right on Rojas' chin and Rojas goes down like a sack of potatoes. That's a wrap.

Official decision: Bilal Hasan def. Nilson Rojas by KO (straight right), round 2 (2:28)

Namsrai Batbayar vs. Andre Lima: Batbayar looked very raw in this fight. Lima was able to pick him apart on the feet and stay out of the way of all of Batbayar's very telegraphed power punches and kicks. Lima was cruising in the third and, after Batbayar whiffed on a punch, he jumped the guillotine and used that to take home the victory.

Official decision: Andre Lima def. Namsrai Batbayar by submission (guillotine), round 3 (3:03)

Rei Tsuruya vs. Kevin Borjas: Tsuruya showed off some incredible aggression in this bout. he launched himself at Borjas off the opening bell, got him down and then pummelled him with ground and pound. Borjas was forced into total defense. After taking a lot of punishment on the ground, Borjas was finally able to get up, but Tsuruya took him down again, took his back and then attacked with the choke. He had Borjas' arm pinned with his leg and once he started to squeeze it was game over.

Official decision: Rei Tsuruya def. Kevin Borjas by submission (rear naked choke), round 1 (4:14)

Jack Jenkins vs. Sean Woodson: Jenkins had a lot of trouble with Woodson's size and reach in the first round. In the second he managed to sweep Woodson on the ground and spend a lot of time on top. That set up a pivotal third round. In the third, Jenkins was able to crash through range and land some shots and keep Woodson on the fence. Woodson was able to defend well and land some good single shots. I scored the third for Jenkins, but it was a razor thin round.

Official decision: Sean Woodson def. Jack Jenkins by split decision (29-28, 28-29, 29-28)

Francesco Nuzzi vs. Xiao Long: Long came in hot, flying at Nuzzi with a knee off the opening bell. Nuzzi brushed that off, though. Moments later, Nuzzi caught Long with an eye poke that paused the action. Shortly after the restart Nuzzi caught Long with a hard left and then blitzed him with about a dozen shots that had Long flailing on the canvas. Herb Dean stepped in and called the fight, much to Long's dismay (who then almost stumbled out the cage door).

Official decision: Francesco Nuzzi def. Xiao Long by TKO (punches), round 1 (1:00)

Lawrence Lui vs. Hector Santiago: Former kickboxer Santiago showed off his heavy striking in his UFC debut here. He landed on Lui in the first round, but really put his foot on the gas in the second. He rocked Lui with a glancing blow to the head and then stalked him down and dropped him with a straight right to the jaw.

Official decision: Hector Santiago def. Lawrence Lui by KO (punches), round 2 (0:53)

Jingnan Xiong vs. Julia Polastri: Polastri gave us one of the nastiest women's MMA KOs we've seen in UFC. She threw a two punch combo and then followed that with a head kick. Xiong was leaning back from the punches and moved her head right into the kick. She was out before she hit the ground. Polastri would have won a POTN bonus had she made weight for this.

Official decision: Julia Polastri def. Jingnan Xiong by KO (headkick), round 1 (3:06)

Ding Meng vs. Cam Nelson: Nelson made this a boring fight and that was bad for Ding and the crowd in Shanghai. Ding had the striking advantage, but his total lack of takedown defense ruined this fight for him. Nelson took him down with ease in the first two rounds. Nelson got tired in the third, but Ding wasn't able to take advantage of that.

Official decision: Cam Nelson def. Ding Meng by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-28)

articles.summary: Returning to London after a one-year hiatus, All In will shine the spotlight on many of AEW's biggest stars and rivalries on Sunday.
articles.body:
Returning to London after a one-year hiatus, All In will shine the spotlight on many of AEW's biggest stars and rivalries on Sunday.

Eight titles are scheduled to be defended on the main card, including Kenny Omega putting the AEW World Championship on the line against Will Ospreay, and Willow Nightingale defending the AEW Women's World Championship against Mercedes Moné.

Other huge names such as Jon Moxley, MJF, Adam Copeland, Christian Cage and The Young Bucks will also be in action as part of what looks to be the most stacked pay-per-view card of the year for AEW.

MJF Sounds Off on Andrade, Pro Wrestling, More 🗣️

Here is everything you need to know about AEW All In 2026, including the projected match order and which bouts you won't want to miss.

When: Sunday, Aug. 30 at 1 p.m. ET (Zero Hour pre-show starts at 11:30 a.m. ET)

Watch: HBO Max, Prime Video, DAZN, Fubo, PPV.com

AEW All In Card and Projected Match Order

Pre Show AEW World Trios Championship Roulette Royale: "Hangman" Adam Page & Brodido (Bandido & Brody King) (c) vs. Bang Bang Gang (Jay White & The Gunns) vs. The Conglomeration (Orange Cassidy, Kyle O'Reilly & Roderick Strong) vs. Death Riders (Claudio Castagnoli, Pac & Wheeler Yuta) vs. The Demand (Ricochet, Bishop Kaun & Toa Liona) vs. The Dogs (Gabe Kidd, David Finlay & Clark Connors) vs. TBA

AEW Women's World Tag Team Championship: Divine Dominion (Megan Bayne & Lena Kross) (c) vs. Brawling Birds (Jamie Hayter & Alex Windsor)

TNT Championship Falls Count Anywhere: Kevin Knight (c) vs. Darby Allin

Men's Casino Gauntlet Match: MJF vs. Andrade El Idolo vs. Tommaso Ciampa vs. Mark Davis vs. TBA

Continental Championship: Jon Moxley (c) vs. Nigel McGuinness

International Championship Three-Way Match: Kyle Fletcher (c) vs. Konosuke Takeshita vs. Kazuchika Okada

AEW World Tag Team Championship: Adam Copeland & Christian Cage (c) vs. The Young Bucks

AEW Women's World Championship: Willow Nightingale (c) vs. Mercedes Moné

AEW World Championship: Kenny Omega (c) vs. Will Ospreay

In the likely main event of All In, Will Ospreay will attempt to become AEW world champion for the first time in front of his hometown fans.

Ospreay won the Men's Owen Hart Cup in order to receive a world title opportunity at All In, and Omega later beat MJF for the AEW World Championship to set the stage for one of the most highly anticipated matches in AEW history.

Omega and Ospreay have faced off in one-on-one matches before, and while they were undoubtedly entertaining, the stakes have never been higher than they will be at All In.

Ospreay has a chance to finally ascend to the top of the mountain in AEW, and doing so in front of his countrymen and countrywomen would unquestionably make it even more special.

Omega figures to have his fair share of supporters as well, and it could make for an explosive atmosphere and one of the best matches of the year in pro wrestling.

Like Ospreay, Mercedes Moné has a chance to end a long journey to the top at All In if she can beat Willow Nightingale for the AEW Women's World Championship.

Mercedes' AEW run has largely been dominant, complete with the longest TBS Championship reign of all time, but she has faltered when having the opportunity to become AEW women's world champ.

At All In, arguably her biggest rival stands in her way, as Willow won the women's title last month to set up another high-stakes match between her and The CEO.

Nightingale owns multiple wins over Moné in her career, including beating her for the TBS title back in December.

Another victory against Mercedes on the All In stage would further cement Nightingale's status as the face of the AEW women's division, but she figures to get the very best Moné has to offer on Sunday.

In a tag team dream match that has been talked about for years, Adam Copeland and Christian Cage will defend the AEW World Tag Team Championships against The Young Bucks at All In.

Given their status as one of the most decorated tag teams in WWE history, Cope and Cage are firmly in the conversation as one of the best tag teams of all time, and The Young Bucks are looking to enter that conversation as well.

While they have dominated the tag scene in multiple companies over the years, beating a team with Cope and Cage's accolades at Wembley Stadium would be among the greatest accomplishments of The Young Bucks' careers.

As for the match itself, the two teams couldn't be much more different stylistically, but they both thrive when it comes to earning the support of the fans.

Much like Omega vs. Ospreay, the crowd may be split for Cope and Cage vs. The Bucks, and it should make for a raucous environment at Wembley.

articles.standfirst: El peleador chino cazó con un uppercut al primo de Khabib en el UFc Shanghái y se postula como próximo retador en el peso gallo
articles.summary: El peleador chino cazó con un uppercut al primo de Khabib en el UFc Shanghái y se postula como próximo retador en el peso gallo
articles.body: Sorpresón mayúsculo el que se acaba de vivir en el UFC Shanghái, donde Song Yadong (24-9-1, 1NC) ha noqueado a Umar Nurmagomedov (20-2) con un uppercut que le ha permitido ser profeta en su tierra y mejorar notablemente una noche aciaga para los peleadores chinos. La velada en sí estuvo llena de highlights, y la victoria del peleador chino le postula como uno de los próximos retadores al título tras convertirse en el primer peleador que noquea al primo de Khabib Nurmagomedov. Umar era el gran favorito para el combate, e incluso algunos consideraban que esta pelea sería un mero trámite antes de volver a pelear por el título o contra Merab Dvalishvili. Así parecía que sería tras el primer asalto, donde Nurmagomedov consiguió dominar con los derribos. Sin embargo, en el segundo round Yadong le estaba esperando y le colocó un uppercut entre el cuello y la parte posterior de la oreja que dejó inconsciente a Umar. Increíble. El evento co estelar fue un jarro de agua fría para el público chino, ya que Denise Gomes (13-3) volvió a demostrar por qué es una de las mayores pegadoras de peso paja tras noquear a Yan Xiaonan (19-6, 1NC) con un brutal codazo en el primer asalto que supuso una de las mejores finalizaciones de la velada. Con 26 años, la brasileña ya suma cinco victorias consecutivas en la UFC, y acaba de noquear a toda una ex contendiente al título -la segunda de su carrera- como la peleadora china, por lo que la oportunidad titular está más cerca que nunca para ella. De hecho, ya es la mayor noqueadora de la historia de peso paja de la UFC -cuatro K.O.- empatada con Jessica Andrade. Por otro lado, Kai Asakura (23-6) parece haber encontrado su zona de comfort en el peso gallo de la UFC, donde ya suma dos finalizaciones seguidas. La de hoy ha sido tras una gran patada a la cabeza a Aoriqileng (26-14), que nada pudo hacer ante el ex campeón de Rizin. La UFC le fichó para competir directamente por el título de peso mosca ante Alexandre Pantoja, pero ha quedado claro que su categoría son las 135 libras, donde los cortes de peso no son tan duros y se encuentra con mejores sensaciones. La primera victoria para un peleador chino la protagonizó Liu Ce (4-1) ante Levi Rodrigues (5-2, 1NC) en peso semipesado. Ambos son pegadores natos, por lo que se esperaba un combate corto y así fue. Ce noqueó al brasileño con una increíble derecha que le apagó las luces después de dar un recital en el primer asalto que le permite debutar a lo grande en UFC y demostrar que en esta categoria hay pocos strikers como él, ya que viene del Kickboxing y el K1. El gran debut de la noche fue el de Bilal Hassan (10-0, 1NC), que hace menos de tres semanas se ganó su contrato en la UFC con un increíble K.O. en las Dana White's Contender Series. El peleador indonesio tiene una pegada impropia del peso mosca, noquea con un solo golpe e hizo lo propio ante Nilson Rojas (9-1) en el segundo asalto con una combinación devastadora que le mandó a la lona. Además, Hassan es de esos chicos con un aura increíble de superestrella, y fan acérrimo de Michael Jackson, por lo que no podía fallar en el día de su cumpleaños. La cartelera preliminar estuvo plagada de finalizaciones. Una de ellas fue la sumisión de André Lima (12-1) ante Namsrai Batbayar (10-1) con una guillotina en el tercer asalto en un combate que ya iba dominando de por sí y que le permite redimirse de su primera derrota profesional hace unos meses contra Kevin Borjas (11-6). De hecho, el propio Borjas también compitió en esta cartelera, y fue sometido por Rei Tsuruya (12-1) con un mataleón en el primer asalto, lo que permite al japonés meterse de lleno en el top 15 de la división de peso mosca. Otro de los mejores K.O. de las preliminares fue el del debutante Francesco Nuzzi (12-2, 2NC) ante Xiao Long (27-12) en el primer asalto. De hecho, en las cuatro primeras peleas hubo tres debutantes y los tres sellaron su victoria, mientras que los peleadores chinos no pudieron conseguir ni una sola victoria en la cartelera preliminar con cuatro derrotas.
